subject: Bridge provisioning cadence & credentialing for POC environment
messages:
From: Ben Lee <ben.lee@avasystems.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC access — next steps and tight timeline

Thanks, Tessa — excited to push this forward. We have internal approval to start a 4-week POC next week. High level asks from our infra team:

- Org setup (we need to provision a test org and invite 3 service accounts)
- API keys scoped to the evaluation project (no prod tokens)
- IP allowlist entries for our staging CIDRs (list coming in separate email)
- VPC peering if possible (we can provide VPC IDs)

Can you confirm Redwood can deliver those pieces within the first 72 hours of kick-off? If not, let us know which items will be staged. Also attaching our internal timeline.

Ben
Head of Platform — Ava Systems

Attachment: avasys-poc-timeline.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Lee <ben.lee@avasystems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC access — next steps and tight timeline

Ben — thanks and congrats on approval. Short answer: yes, we can meet the 72-hour floor for basic access (org invite + API keys + IP allowlist). VPC peering is usually a 48–72 hour inbound cloud-side change but often depends on the customer's cloud team to accept vs our infra to provision routes. Proposed cadence: 

1) Day 0 (kick-off): create evaluation org, invite service accounts, share initial API key scope (test-only).
2) Day 1: populate IP allowlist (we'll need the CIDRs), deliver network-allowlist-template.csv for your infra to fill.
3) Day 2–3: initiate VPC peering request from our side; coordinate acceptance window with your cloud team.
4) Day 3: share a scoped token rotation policy and short runbook for credential handling.

I'll attach a draft MAP (mutual action plan) and the allowlist template. Karthik / Marissa — can you own the org creation and key scoping? I'll coordinate with Ben on peering windows.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-map-draft.pdf (attachment stub); network-allowlist-template.csv (attachment stub)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: RE: POC access — next steps and tight timeline

Tessa — I can build the evaluation org and pre-configure three service accounts (ingest, eval-runner, webhook) by EOD tomorrow. Questions for Ben:

- What exact roles do you want attached to the service accounts? (e.g., read-only model metadata, generation-only, token-management disabled)
- For API keys: do you want per-service-account keys or a single scoped key for the POC? We recommend per-service-account keys for traceability.

I'll also prepare an API key naming convention (ave-<env>-<role>-yyyymmdd) and a short rotation schedule. Marissa — can you validate the token TTL and revocation steps with infra-ops?

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Lee <ben.lee@avasystems.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC access — next steps and tight timeline

Karthik — thanks, that sounds good. Roles: 

- ingest: write-only to the eval ingest endpoint
- eval-runner: generation + embeddings read
- webhook: minimal read-only for callback validation

We'll do per-service-account keys. Attached is our staging CIDR list and VPC IDs. Our cloud ops are available Monday morning (Nov 30) for the peering acceptance window. If Redwood can initiate the peering on Monday 09:00–11:00 PST, we can accept and perform validation tests same day.

Confirming: staging CIDRs (10.40.0.0/16, 10.41.0.0/16), VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d

Ben
Attachment: avasys-staging-cidrs.csv (attachment stub)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Lee <ben.lee@avasystems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC access — next steps and tight timeline

Ben — all set. Quick summary and confirmations so everyone has one source of truth: 

- Org and service accounts: created (eval org ID: eval-avasys-9201). Invitations sent to the three service-account emails you provided.
- API keys: issued per service account and uploaded to the evaluation org; keys labelled ave-eval-ingest-20261128, ave-eval-runner-20261128, ave-eval-webhook-20261128.
- IP allowlist: we've added 10.40.0.0/16 and 10.41.0.0/16 to the staging allowlist. Please confirm connectivity to token endpoint.
- VPC peering: peering request submitted from our VPC (vpc-8d7f3c1a) at 09:00 PST on Mon Nov 30. Please have your cloud ops accept the request during the 09:00–11:00 PST window. We'll run a basic connectivity smoke test post-accept.

Next steps: Ben to accept peering on Monday; once accepted we'll run a scripted smoke (token auth, simple generation, webhook callback) and report back. I've attached the DocuSign mutual-action-plan signature packet; please sign the MUP so legal has a record of the access terms.

If anything slips, we'll fall back to scoped tunneling for the first 48 hours so you can start eval traffic immediately.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: docusign-mup-template.pdf (DocuSign link: https://redwood.ai/docusign/exec/9201); runbook link: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/POC-Runbook-ava
